raw_response.overlap_rationale: Study A (Quattrochi et al., 2025, PLOS Medicine) and Study B (Quattrochi et al., 2021, BMJ Global Health) are companion follow-up reports of the exact same cluster-randomized controlled trial (AEARCTR-0004648) evaluating the DRC's national Healthy Villages and Schools (Villages et Ecoles Assainis, VEA) programme across the exact same 121 clusters (50 treatment clusters, 71 control clusters; 332 randomized rural villages) in four provinces (Kongo Central, Kasai, Kasai Central, and South Kivu). Study B reports the short-term (median 5-month post-intervention) survey wave conducted in October–December 2019 among 1,312 households (4 per village) and village/WASH leaders across 328 villages. Study A explicitly cites Study B as the first-round 5-month follow-up (Ref. 26) and reports the long-term (median 3.6-year post-intervention) survey wave conducted between November 2022 and February/April 2023 across 329 of the same trial villages, interviewing 3,283 households—comprising 1,133 re-interviewed respondents (86% of Study B's 1,312 households, plus replacement/new-respondent Wave 1 households) alongside 1,970 newly sampled households (6 per village). Because both studies estimate intention-to-treat effects of the identical randomized intervention on the identical 121 village clusters (with 86% household panel retention plus augmented household sampling at Wave 2) across overlapping outcomes (improved water source, improved sanitation facility, WASH/water governance index, water satisfaction, handwashing/hygiene behavior, cost of water, school attendance, and child diarrhea/health), treating them as independent studies in evidence synthesis creates a high risk of double-counting the same trial.
raw_response.study_a_sample_and_data: Cluster-randomized controlled trial (AEARCTR-0004648; PACTR202102616421588) of the 'Healthy Villages' component of DRC's Healthy Villages and Schools (VEA) programme in four provinces (Kongo Central, Kasai, Kasai Central, South Kivu): 332 rural villages grouped into 121 clusters (50 intervention clusters with 146 villages; 71 control clusters with 186 villages), randomized March–June 2018. Long-term (median 3.6-year post-intervention) follow-up survey conducted November 2022–April 2023 (field interviews Nov 24, 2022–Feb 10, 2023) across 329 villages and N = 3,283 households (head woman interviewed), comprising 1,133 re-interviewed respondents from the 2019 5-month follow-up (plus 140 replacement households and 39 new respondents in Wave 1 households) and 1,970 newly sampled households (6 per village), with child diarrhea assessed for N = 4,072 children under 5 (in 2,466 households), length-for-age Z-score measured for N = 2,142 children (in 2,374 eligible households), WASH institutions index measured in N = 329 villages, plus water-point and household E. coli/coliform testing and structured handwashing observations.
raw_response.study_b_sample_and_data: Cluster-randomized controlled trial (AEARCTR-0004648) of the 'Healthy Villages' component of DRC's Healthy Villages and Schools (VEA) programme in the same four provinces (Kongo Central, Kasai, Kasai Central, South Kivu): 332 rural villages grouped into 121 clusters (50 treatment clusters, 71 control clusters). Short-term (median 5-month / 151-day post-intervention) follow-up survey conducted October 11–December 23, 2019 across N = 328 villages (145 treatment, 183 control) and N = 1,312 households (4 per village; 580 intervention, 732 control; head woman interviewed), alongside a concurrent village chief and WASH committee leadership survey (N = 328 villages) and child health module (N = 1,388 children aged 10–59 months).
